A tutorial on conducting GWAS (Marees et al., 2018)

rows.right: QC: drop samples and SNPs with a low call rate

wrong.text: Run the association test on the raw genotypes
wrong.why: Raw calls give false hits: quality control comes first.

rows.right: plink --bfile data --maf 0.01 --make-bed --out qc

wrong.text: plink --bfile data --maf 0.5 --make-bed --out qc
wrong.why: --maf 0.5 keeps only SNPs whose minor allele is at 50%: almost none.

wrong.text: rm -rf raw/
wrong.why: Never delete the raw data: QC writes new files.

rows.right: PCA to see population structure

wrong.text: Fine-map the top hit
wrong.why: There are no hits yet: fine-mapping comes after the association test.

rows.right: Impute untyped variants from a reference panel

wrong.text: Average the genotypes along each chromosome
wrong.why: Not a step: imputation fills in untyped variants from a reference panel.

rows.right: Test association with covariates and ancestry PCs

wrong.text: Leave out the covariates to get more hits
wrong.why: Without ancestry PCs, population structure shows up as false positives.

wrong.text: Test only the SNPs you expect to matter
wrong.why: A GWAS tests every variant: choosing first biases it.

rows.right: Call a hit at p < 5 × 10⁻⁸

wrong.text: Call every SNP with p < 0.05 a hit
wrong.why: With a million tests, 0.05 gives about 50,000 false hits.

rows.right: Clump by LD, then fine-map each locus

wrong.text: Report every significant SNP as its own discovery
wrong.why: Neighbouring SNPs in LD carry the same signal: one locus, not many.

source.title: Current best practices in single-cell RNA-seq analysis (Luecken & Theis, 2019)

rows.right: cellranger count: reads to a count matrix

wrong.text: Cluster the raw FASTQ files
wrong.why: Reads must be aligned and counted per cell first.

rows.right: Remove empty droplets and ambient RNA

wrong.text: Keep every barcode, empty droplets too
wrong.why: Most barcodes are empty droplets: they would form fake cells.

rows.right: Filter cells by genes detected and % mitochondrial reads

wrong.text: Drop every cell with any mitochondrial read
wrong.why: All cells have some: only a high fraction marks dying cells.

rows.right: sc.pp.normalize_total(adata); sc.pp.log1p(adata)

wrong.text: sc.tl.leiden(adata) before normalising
wrong.why: Clustering raw counts groups cells by sequencing depth, not by type.

rows.right: Variable genes, then PCA, neighbours and UMAP

wrong.text: UMAP straight on all 30,000 genes
wrong.why: Slow and noisy: reduce to variable genes and PCA first.

rows.right: Cluster (Leiden), then find marker genes

wrong.text: Name the cell types before clustering
wrong.why: Types are named from the markers of each cluster, so clusters come first.

source.title: RNA-seq workflow: gene-level exploratory analysis and differential expression (Bioconductor)

rows.right: Check read quality with FastQC

wrong.text: Start with the volcano plot
wrong.why: A volcano plot needs results: you start from the reads.

rows.right: Quantify reads per gene (Salmon or STAR + featureCounts)

wrong.text: Count reads per chromosome
wrong.why: Expression is measured per gene or transcript, not per chromosome.

rows.right: Import raw counts into DESeq2

wrong.text: Give DESeq2 counts you've already normalised to TPM
wrong.why: DESeq2 models raw counts; it normalises them itself.

rows.right: Look at a PCA of samples for outliers and batches

wrong.text: Drop samples until the PCA looks tidy
wrong.why: Removing samples without a reason is cherry-picking.

rows.right: Fit the design, e.g. ~ batch + condition

wrong.text: Leave the known batch out of the design
wrong.why: An unmodelled batch hides or fakes differences.

rows.right: Keep genes at adjusted p (FDR) < 0.05

wrong.text: Keep genes at raw p < 0.05
wrong.why: Over 20,000 genes, raw p-values give hundreds of false positives.

rows.right: Align reads to the reference with BWA-MEM

wrong.text: Call variants straight from the FASTQ
wrong.why: Variants are called from reads placed on the reference.

rows.right: Sort the BAM and mark duplicates

wrong.text: Keep PCR duplicates: more reads, more evidence
wrong.why: Duplicates repeat one molecule and inflate confidence.

rows.right: Recalibrate base qualities (BQSR)

wrong.text: Set every base quality to 40
wrong.why: Faking qualities hides real sequencing errors.

rows.right: Call per sample with HaplotypeCaller in GVCF mode

wrong.text: Merge all BAMs into one sample first
wrong.why: Merging loses which sample has which variant.

rows.right: Joint-genotype the GVCFs together

wrong.text: Genotype each sample alone and paste the VCFs
wrong.why: Joint calling tells a missing call from a reference call.

rows.right: Filter variants (VQSR or hard filters)

wrong.text: Publish every raw call
wrong.why: Unfiltered calls include many artefacts.

rows.right: Hold out a test set before anything else

wrong.text: Tune the model on all the data, then test on it
wrong.why: Testing on data the model saw measures memory, not skill.

rows.right: Start with a simple baseline

wrong.text: Start with the biggest network you can fit
wrong.why: Without a baseline you can't tell if the big model helps.

rows.right: Fit preprocessing on the training set only

wrong.text: Scale using the mean of all the data
wrong.why: That leaks test information into training.

rows.right: Choose settings by cross-validation

wrong.text: Choose settings by test-set score
wrong.why: Then the test set is no longer unseen.

rows.right: Report the metric on the untouched test set, once

wrong.text: Report the best of many test runs
wrong.why: Picking the best run overstates performance.

rows.right: Fork the repository

wrong.text: Push straight to the project's main branch
wrong.why: You can't, and shouldn't: changes go through a pull request.

rows.right: git clone your fork

wrong.text: Download a ZIP and edit it
wrong.why: A ZIP has no history: you can't make a pull request from it.

rows.right: git switch -c fix-typo

wrong.text: Commit on main
wrong.why: A branch keeps your change separate and easy to update.

rows.right: Commit with a clear message

wrong.text: Commit with the message "stuff"
wrong.why: Reviewers read the history: say what changed and why.

rows.right: git push origin fix-typo

wrong.text: git push --force origin main
wrong.why: Force-pushing main rewrites shared history.

rows.right: Open a pull request and describe the change

wrong.text: Email the maintainer the files
wrong.why: A pull request lets them review, discuss and merge.

source.title: Ten simple rules for better figures (Rougier et al., 2014)

rows.right: Decide the one message the figure must show

wrong.text: Put every result into one figure
wrong.why: A figure with no single message shows nothing clearly.

rows.right: Choose the plot that fits the data (points for few samples)

wrong.text: Use a bar chart of means for n = 3
wrong.why: Bars hide the spread: show the points.

rows.right: Use a colour-blind-safe palette

wrong.text: Use red and green for the two groups
wrong.why: About 1 in 12 men can't tell red from green.

rows.right: Label axes with names and units

wrong.text: Leave the axes as x and y
wrong.why: Readers can't interpret an unlabeled axis.

rows.right: Export as vector (PDF or SVG) at final size

wrong.text: Screenshot it at screen resolution
wrong.why: Screenshots blur when printed or zoomed.

rows.right: Trim primers and check read quality

wrong.text: Count species from raw reads
wrong.why: Primers and poor bases distort every later step.

rows.right: Denoise into ASVs (DADA2)

wrong.text: Cluster everything at 80% identity
wrong.why: So loose a threshold merges distinct taxa.

rows.right: Assign taxonomy with a trained classifier (SILVA)

wrong.text: Name taxa by sequence length
wrong.why: Length says nothing about which organism it is.

rows.right: Rarefy or use compositional methods before comparing

wrong.text: Compare raw read counts between samples
wrong.why: Samples have different depths: raw counts aren't comparable.

rows.right: Test differences in diversity and abundance

wrong.text: Report the most abundant taxon as the effect
wrong.why: Abundance alone isn't a difference between groups.

items.label: Off-by-one
items.why: A loop that runs one time too many or too few.

items.label: Typo
items.why: A misspelt name: the code calls something that doesn't exist.

items.label: Memory leak
items.why: Memory that's taken and never given back.

items.label: Race condition
items.why: Two things running at once, and the result depends on which wins.

items.label: Wrong path
items.why: A file path that only exists on one computer.

items.label: Silent NaN
items.why: A missing value that spreads quietly through every sum.

items.label: Infinite loop
items.why: A loop whose end condition is never met.

items.label: Hard-coded seed
items.why: Every run looks random but is the same, or results change with no seed at all.

items.label: Null pointer
items.why: Using something that was never set.

items.label: Integer overflow
items.why: A number too big for its type wraps around.

items.label: Data leak
items.why: Test data used in training: scores look better than they are.

items.label: Mixed-up columns
items.why: Two columns swapped, so every result is about the wrong variable.

items.why: The last line never closes its bracket: print(top.head(10)).
A comparison needs <= (or ==): a single = inside filter() is an error.
range(1, ...) starts at 1, so TP53, the first gene, is never printed.
done must start its own command: gzip "$f"; done, or put done on its own line.
It divides by len(x), one number, instead of len(xs), the list.
mean() of a vector with NA is NA: use mean(x, na.rm = TRUE).
Arrays of length 3 and 2 can't be added: shapes must match or broadcast.
COUNT(*) with gene needs GROUP BY gene, or the query fails.
scores[name] doesn't exist yet: use scores.get(name, 0) + 1 or a Counter.
R names are case-sensitive: the column is ratio, not Ratio.
samtools sort takes one file at a time: loop over the SAM files.
Scaling with all the data leaks test information: fit the scaler on the training rows only.
An if needs a colon at the end: if line.startswith('>'):
If x is empty, 1:length(x) is c(1, 0) and the loop runs twice: use seq_along(x).
If OUTDIR is empty, this becomes rm -rf /*: check the variable or use ${OUTDIR:?}.
random.seed() with no value resets to a random seed: the run is no longer repeatable.
Nothing equals NULL: use WHERE tissue IS NULL.
list.sort() sorts in place and returns None: use sorted(values).
The + must end the previous line, not start the next: R ends the command early.
A FASTQ record is 4 lines, not 2: divide by 4.
